label: Equal per-assertion probability, different joint: ERROR_DEPENDENCE_1 vs ERROR_DEPENDENCE_2
paraphrase: For 0<q<1 and n≥2 assertions, in every shared-only profile (ERROR_DEPENDENCE_1: local conditions almost sure, shared condition probability q) each assertion and all of them together have probability q and at-least-one-false has 1−q; in every isolated-errors profile (ERROR_DEPENDENCE_2: shared condition almost sure, local probability q) each assertion has probability q but all together have q^n, strictly less than q. Also, for any measure and any nonempty index, conditioning on the intersection of repeated copies of one evidence event equals conditioning on it once. Per-assertion support therefore does not determine joint support: q^n is what the isolated regime yields and does not follow from q and n alone. When restatements of one claim are modeled as the same event, repeating them supplies no further confirmation; that weight rests on the modeling choice, since the conditioning identity itself is definitional. No probability is assigned to any corpus statement.
